title: EACH THE BLESSING APPROPRIATE TO HIM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them when he blessed them, giving each the blessing appropriate to him." — Gen 49:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Giving each the blessing appropriate to him."

That is a striking summary, especially when you remember what Jacob actually said. Reuben lost his position. Simeon and Levi were told they would be scattered. These were not comfortable words. And yet the text calls the whole thing a blessing.

A word can be hard and still be a blessing. Sometimes the most loving thing anyone ever says to us is the thing we least wanted to hear.

Notice too the word "appropriate." Jacob did not say the same thing to all twelve. He spoke to each son as that particular son needed. Some received warning, some encouragement, some a warm word about their gifts. Real love is specific.

God deals with us this way. Hebrews says the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and that no discipline seems pleasant at the time, but later it produces a harvest of righteousness and peace (Heb 12:6, 11).

If God has spoken a hard word into your life, do not assume He has withdrawn His love. He may be blessing you in exactly the way you need.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has a hard word ever turned out to be a blessing in your life?
2. Do you speak to people generically, or attend to what each one needs?
3. Is there something God has been saying that you have resisted because it stings?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your love is honest with me. Help me receive Your hard words as blessing, and to speak to others with the same specific care. Amen.
